mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last three weeks and dropped sharply (-14 points) in the most recent week, indicating a persistent downward momentum in retail and recreation activity that will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks absent any reversal signal.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -22.0 to -38.4 over four weeks with largest drop in the latest week
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the downward momentum reversed despite no observed catalyst.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility falls below -60 percent from baseline, commuters and shoppers sharply curtail non-essential trips requiring public transport, which mechanically suppresses retail and recreation visits for roughly two weeks following the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -60 percent from baseline in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -66.0 in week t-0w, crossing the -60 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite TRANSIT remaining below -60, indicating transit suppression no longer transmits to retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compound each other: fewer commuters moving through transit hubs near workplaces reduces incidental retail stops, so joint deterioration in both series produces a larger drag on RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES (-22.0 to -31.4) and TRANSIT (-50.4 to -66.0) declined steadily over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decline over the next 4 weeks is no larger than what a single-series (WORKPLACES-only or TRANSIT-only) linear model would predict, indicating no amplifying interaction.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous rise in RESIDENTIAL and fall in WORKPLACES signals that local authorities and residents are re-entering a restriction-tightening regime (akin to localized lockdown measures), which will further compress retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks as people shift back to staying home.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 11.6 to 17.7 while WORKPLACES fell from -22.0 to -31.4 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues rising and WORKPLACES continues falling, indicating the restriction-regime linkage to retail mobility has broken down.

mechanism_narrative: Despite being peak summer when outdoor and park activity typically rises, PARKS mobility has fallen sharply in the latest week, indicating that restriction-driven caution is overriding seasonal outdoor-activity incentives; this suppressed seasonal effect will also hold back the leisure component of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -15.4 (t-2w) to -37.9 (t-0w) despite the summer season
regime_hint: summer season under reimposed mobility restrictions
failure_condition: PARKS and RETAIL_REC both rebound within the next four weeks even without any change in restriction policy, showing the seasonal effect was not actually suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility exceeding 5 points signals a shift toward precautionary, consolidated essential-only shopping trips, which reduces discretionary retail and recreation visits within the following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-over-week decline exceeds 5 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped from -2.9 to -11.1 between t-1w and t-0w, an 8.2 point decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week immediately following a GROCERY_PHARM drop greater than 5 points, indicating no behavioral spillover.

mechanism_narrative: Coordinated movement of WORKPLACES down, TRANSIT down, and RESIDENTIAL up over consecutive weeks is a composite signature of reinstated containment measures (e.g., local lockdowns or curfews); this joint policy signature predicts a sustained four-week decline in RETAIL_REC beyond what any single series implies.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES, TRANSIT fell while RESIDENTIAL rose in all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline further over 4 weeks even as all three series continue in their composite direction, falsifying the compound policy-signature mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: An acute acceleration where RETAIL_REC drops more than 10 points week-over-week while WORKPLACES also falls in the same week indicates a sudden shock (e.g., new restriction announcement) whose short-term effect further depresses RETAIL_REC over the immediate following week before any stabilization.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-over-week drop exceeds 10 points while WORKPLACES also falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell 14 points (-24.4 to -38.4) while WORKPLACES fell 1.8 points (-29.6 to -31.4) in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds or stabilizes in the week immediately after the joint shock condition is met, indicating the acute-shock mechanism does not persist short-term.
